title: Chicken Tikka Masala
intro: Charred yogurt-marinated chicken folded into a silky, spiced tomato and cream sauce.
ingredients: 700 g (1½ lb) boneless chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm chunks
steps: Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, half the garlic and ginger, 1 teaspoon garam masala, 1 teaspoon cumin, the turmeric and half the chilli powder in a bowl. Add the chicken, coat well and leave to marinate for at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.

Heat the grill to its highest setting. Spread the chicken on a lined tray and grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until the edges are charred and the meat is just cooked. Set aside with any juices.
Warm the oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the remaining garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the remaining garam masala, cumin, chilli powder and the paprika and stir for 30 seconds so the spices bloom in the oil.
Tip in the chopped tomatoes and tomato purée with 100 ml (scant ½ cup) water. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and darker in colour.
Pour in the cream, add the grilled chicken and its juices, and simmer gently for 5 minutes until the sauce coats the meat. Season to taste.
Scatter with coriander and serve with rice or naan.

title: Butter Chicken
intro: A mild, buttery Delhi classic where tender chicken sits in a smooth tomato sauce enriched with cream.
ingredients: 700 g (1½ lb) boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
steps: Combine the yogurt, lemon juice, half the garlic and ginger, 1 teaspoon garam masala, the cumin, chilli powder and turmeric. Stir in the chicken and leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the grill to high. Lay the chicken on a lined tray and grill for 8 to 10 minutes, turning halfway, until lightly charred. Keep to one side.
Melt half the butter in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft, then add the remaining garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and a pinch of salt and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Blend with a stick blender until completely smooth.
Return the sauce to the pan with the cream, the remaining garam masala and the fenugreek leaves rubbed between your palms. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the grilled chicken and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes until cooked through and the sauce is glossy. Stir in the remaining butter just before serving.
Taste for salt and serve with basmati rice or naan.

title: Pad Thai
intro: Bangkok's famous street noodle dish, tossed quickly with prawns, egg and a tangy tamarind sauce.
ingredients: 150 g (5 oz) dried flat rice noodles
2 tbsp palm sugar or soft brown sugar
100 g (3½ oz) firm tofu, cut into small cubes
3 spring onions or garlic chives, cut into 3 cm lengths
40 g (¼ cup) roasted peanuts, roughly crushed
steps: Soak the rice noodles in warm water for 15 to 20 minutes until pliable but still firm, then drain.
Stir together the tamarind paste, fish sauce and sugar in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat. Fry the garlic and shallots for 30 seconds, then add the tofu and cook for 2 minutes until lightly golden.
Add the prawns and stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes until they turn pink.
Push everything to one side, crack the eggs into the empty space and scramble them for about 30 seconds before mixing through.
Add the drained noodles and the sauce and toss over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles are tender and have soaked up the liquid.
Throw in most of the beansprouts and the spring onions and toss for a final 30 seconds.
Serve topped with the crushed peanuts, remaining beansprouts, lime wedges and chilli flakes.

title: Pho Bo (Beef Noodle Soup)
intro: A clear, fragrant beef broth steeped with charred onion and spices, poured over rice noodles and thin raw beef.
ingredients: 1.5 kg (3¼ lb) beef bones (marrow and knuckle)
10 cm piece fresh ginger, halved lengthways
400 g (14 oz) dried flat rice noodles
250 g (9 oz) beef sirloin, very thinly sliced
Beansprouts, Thai basil, coriander, spring onions and lime wedges, to serve
Sliced red chilli and hoisin sauce, to serve
steps: Cover the bones with cold water in a large stockpot, bring to the boil and boil hard for 10 minutes. Drain, rinse the bones and scrub out the pot.
Char the onion halves and ginger directly over a gas flame or under a hot grill for about 10 minutes until blackened in patches.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander seeds and cardamom in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant, then tie them in a muslin bag.
Return the bones to the pot with the brisket, charred onion and ginger, spice bag, fish sauce, sugar and salt. Cover with about 4 litres (17 cups) of water and bring to a bare simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 3 hours, skimming any foam from the surface. Lift out the brisket after 1 hour 30 minutes, once tender, and cool it in cold water before slicing thinly.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve, discard the solids, and taste for salt and fish sauce. Keep it at a rolling simmer.
Cook the rice noodles according to the packet, drain and divide between six deep bowls. Top with sliced brisket and the raw sirloin slices.
Ladle the boiling broth over the beef so it cooks instantly. Serve with the herbs, beansprouts, lime, chilli and hoisin on the side.

title: Shoyu Ramen
intro: A soy-seasoned ramen with a clear chicken broth, springy noodles, soft eggs and slices of braised pork.
ingredients: 1 kg (2¼ lb) chicken wings and backs
500 g (1 lb) pork belly, skin removed, rolled and tied
2 spring onions, plus extra sliced to serve
4 portions fresh ramen noodles (about 500 g / 1 lb)
Nori sheets, bamboo shoots and sesame oil, to serve
steps: Put the chicken, onion, half the garlic, the ginger, spring onions and kombu in a large pot with 3 litres (12½ cups) of cold water. Bring slowly to a simmer, remove the kombu, and simmer gently for 2 hours 30 minutes, skimming often.

Meanwhile, put the pork belly in a snug saucepan with the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, remaining garlic and 250 ml (1 cup) water. Cover and simmer for 1 hour 30 minutes, turning occasionally, until tender. Lift out the pork and keep the braising liquid as your tare.
Boil the eggs for 6 minutes 30 seconds, cool in iced water, peel and soak in a little of the pork braising liquid for at least 30 minutes.
Strain the chicken broth and keep it hot. Slice the pork into thin rounds and halve the eggs.
Cook the ramen noodles in plenty of boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes until just tender, then drain well.
Put 3 tablespoons of the tare in each bowl, top up with about 400 ml (1⅔ cups) hot broth and add the noodles.
Arrange pork slices, egg halves, bamboo shoots, nori and sliced spring onion on top and finish with a few drops of sesame oil.

title: Maki Sushi Rolls
intro: Seasoned rice and fresh fillings rolled in crisp nori and sliced into neat rounds.
ingredients: 150 g (5 oz) sashimi-grade salmon or tuna, cut into pencil-thick strips
½ cucumber, deseeded and cut into thin batons
Soy sauce, pickled ginger and wasabi, to serve
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs almost clear, then drain and leave for 20 minutes. Put it in a saucepan with 360 ml (1½ cups) water, cover, bring to the boil, then cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Rest off the heat, covered, for 10 minutes.

Warm the rice vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved. Turn the hot rice into a wide bowl, pour the dressing over and fold it through with a cutting motion, fanning to cool it quickly. Cover with a damp cloth.
Lay a sheet of nori shiny side down on a bamboo mat. With wet hands, spread a quarter of the rice over it in an even layer, leaving a 2 cm strip bare at the far edge.
Lay strips of fish, cucumber and avocado in a line across the rice about a third of the way up, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Lift the near edge of the mat and roll it over the filling, tucking firmly, then keep rolling to the bare strip. Dab that strip with water and press to seal.
Repeat with the remaining sheets. Slice each roll into 8 pieces with a sharp knife, wiping the blade with a damp cloth between cuts.
Serve with soy sauce, pickled ginger and wasabi.

title: Egg Fried Rice
intro: The quickest way to turn leftover rice into a satisfying meal, with fluffy egg and spring onions.
ingredients: 400 g (3 cups) cooked and chilled long-grain rice
steps: Break up the cold rice with your fingers so there are no clumps.
Heat half the oil in a wok over high heat, pour in the eggs and scramble for about 30 seconds until just set. Tip onto a plate.
Add the remaining oil, then the garlic, and stir for 10 seconds. Add the rice and toss constantly for 3 to 4 minutes until every grain is hot and starting to crisp at the edges.
Add the peas and most of the spring onions and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return the egg to the wok, pour the soy sauce around the edge so it sizzles, and toss everything together. Finish with the sesame oil and a pinch of white pepper.
Serve immediately with the remaining spring onions on top.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
intro: A Sichuan stir-fry of diced chicken, dried chillies and peanuts in a glossy, tingling sauce.
ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) boneless chicken thighs, cut into 2 cm dice
10 dried red chillies, snipped in half
5 spring onions, white parts cut into 2 cm pieces
steps: Toss the chicken with the light soy sauce, Shaoxing wine and 1 teaspoon of the cornflour and leave for 15 minutes.
Mix the dark soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, remaining cornflour and 3 tablespoons water in a small bowl for the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns for about 30 seconds until fragrant and slightly darkened, without burning them.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion whites and toss for 1 minute.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and cook for about 1 minute until it thickens and clings to the chicken.
Stir in the peanuts and serve straight away with steamed rice.

title: Mapo Tofu
intro: Soft tofu simmered in a fiery, numbing Sichuan sauce with a little minced pork.
ingredients: 450 g (1 lb) soft or silken-firm tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, lightly crushed
2 cm piece fresh ginger, finely chopped
250 ml (1 cup) chicken or vegetable stock
2 tsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water
steps: Slide the tofu cubes into a pan of gently simmering salted water for 2 minutes to firm them up, then drain carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry the pork for 3 to 4 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and slightly crisp.
Lower the heat, add the chilli bean paste and cook for 1 minute until the oil turns red. Stir in the black beans, chilli flakes, garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce and bring to a simmer. Add the tofu and spoon the sauce over it rather than stirring, so the cubes stay whole. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes.
Drizzle in the cornflour slurry and nudge the pan gently for 1 minute until the sauce thickens and turns glossy.
Scatter with the ground Sichuan pepper and spring onions and serve with plenty of steamed rice.

title: Bibimbap
intro: A bowl of warm rice topped with seasoned vegetables, beef and a fried egg, all stirred through chilli paste.
ingredients: 250 g (9 oz) beef sirloin, thinly sliced
2 tbsp sesame oil, plus extra for the vegetables
steps: Rinse the rice, then cook it in 400 ml (1⅔ cups) water: bring to the boil, cover, and simmer on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest for 10 minutes.
Mix the beef with the soy sauce, 1 tablespoon sesame oil, the sugar and half the garlic and leave to marinate while you cook the vegetables.

Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, squeeze dry and toss with a little sesame oil, salt and a pinch of the remaining garlic. Blanch the beansprouts for 2 minutes and dress the same way.
In a frying pan with a splash of oil, stir-fry the carrots for 2 minutes with a pinch of salt and set aside; repeat with the courgette, then the mushrooms, keeping each separate.
Stir-fry the marinated beef in the same pan over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes until browned.
Fry the eggs in a little oil so the yolks stay runny.
Stir the gochujang with the remaining sesame oil and 1 tablespoon water to loosen it.

Divide the rice between four bowls and arrange the vegetables and beef in separate piles on top. Add a fried egg, a spoonful of gochujang sauce and sesame seeds, and mix everything together before eating.

title: Korean Fried Chicken
intro: Twice-fried chicken with a shattering crust, tossed in a sticky, sweet and fiery gochujang glaze.
ingredients: 1 kg (2¼ lb) chicken wings, tips removed and split at the joint
100 g (¾ cup) potato starch or cornflour
steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with the salt and pepper. Mix the potato starch, flour and baking powder in a bowl and toss the chicken in it until evenly coated, shaking off any excess.
Heat 5 cm of oil in a deep, heavy pan to 160 °C (320 °F). Fry the chicken in batches for 8 minutes until pale golden and cooked through, then drain on a rack.
While the chicken rests, stir the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, sugar and garlic together in a small pan. Simmer for 3 minutes until slightly thickened, then stir in the sesame oil.
Raise the oil temperature to 190 °C (375 °F) and fry the chicken a second time in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden and very crisp. Drain again.
Tip the hot chicken into a large bowl, pour over the glaze and toss until every piece is coated.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and spring onions and serve at once, with pickled radish if you have it.

title: Japchae
intro: Chewy sweet potato glass noodles tossed with colourful vegetables, beef and a soy and sesame dressing.
ingredients: 250 g (9 oz) dried sweet potato glass noodles (dangmyeon)
150 g (5 oz) beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
3 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
steps: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, 2 tablespoons of the sesame oil, the garlic and a grind of black pepper. Put the beef in a small bowl with 1 tablespoon of this mixture and leave to marinate; keep the rest for the noodles.
Boil the glass noodles for 6 to 7 minutes until soft and springy, drain, rinse under cold water and snip into shorter lengths with scissors. Toss with the remaining tablespoon of sesame oil.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, cool in cold water, squeeze dry and season with a pinch of salt.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the onion, carrot and red pepper for 3 minutes until just tender but still bright, then tip them out.
In the same pan, stir-fry the mushrooms for 2 minutes, then the beef for 2 to 3 minutes until browned.
Add the noodles, all the cooked vegetables, spinach, spring onions and the reserved sauce to the pan and toss over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until everything is glossy and heated through.
Finish with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Thai Green Curry
intro: A fragrant, fiery coconut curry built on fresh green chillies, lemongrass and Thai basil.
ingredients: 400 ml (14 fl oz) tin coconut milk
500 g (1 lb) boneless chicken thighs, sliced
1 tbsp palm sugar or soft brown sugar
200 g (7 oz) Thai or pea aubergines, halved or whole
steps: Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a wok with the oil over medium heat and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until it splits and looks oily.
Add the curry paste and fry for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells aromatic.
Add the chicken and stir to coat in the paste, cooking for 3 minutes until it loses its pink colour.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the stock, then add the fish sauce, sugar and lime leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Add the aubergines and simmer for 8 minutes, then add the green beans and bamboo shoots and cook for 5 minutes more until the vegetables are tender and the chicken is cooked.
Taste and balance with more fish sauce or sugar as needed. Stir in the Thai basil and sliced chilli.
Serve with jasmine rice.

title: Massaman Curry
intro: A rich, mild southern Thai curry of slow-cooked beef, potatoes and peanuts with warm dry spices.
ingredients: 2 × 400 ml (14 fl oz) tins coconut milk
800 g (1¾ lb) beef chuck, cut into 4 cm chunks
400 g (14 oz) waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into large chunks
2 tbsp palm sugar or soft brown sugar
steps: Heat the oil in a large casserole over medium heat with the thick cream from the top of one tin of coconut milk. Cook for 3 minutes until the oil separates, then add the curry paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the beef and turn it in the paste for 2 to 3 minutes until coated and browned at the edges.
Pour in all the coconut milk, then add the fish sauce, sugar, tamarind, cinnamon, cardamom and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Cover partially and simmer very gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the beef is starting to turn tender.
Add the potatoes, onion and peanuts and simmer uncovered for a further 30 to 40 minutes until the potatoes are soft and the sauce has thickened.
Fish out the cinnamon, cardamom and bay, taste for salt, sweetness and sourness, and adjust.
Serve with jasmine rice and a few extra peanuts on top.

title: Chicken Biryani
intro: Layers of spiced chicken and saffron-scented basmati, steamed together until every grain is fragrant.
ingredients: 800 g (1¾ lb) bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
1 cinnamon stick, 4 green cardamom pods, 4 cloves and 2 bay leaves
Large pinch saffron soaked in 3 tbsp warm milk
Small bunch each fresh mint and coriander, chopped
steps: Mix the yogurt with the garlic, ginger, garam masala, turmeric, chilli powder, green chillies and 1 teaspoon salt. Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 1 hour.

Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and soak it for 30 minutes. Heat the ghee in a large pan and fry the onions over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Remove half for the layers, leaving the rest in the pan.
Add the chicken and its marinade to the onions in the pan and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and the chicken is almost cooked.
Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil with the cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and bay. Add the drained rice and boil for 5 to 6 minutes until the grains are two-thirds cooked, then drain.

Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Spread half the rice over the chicken in the pan, scatter with half the herbs and fried onions, then add the remaining rice, herbs and onions. Drizzle the saffron milk over the top.
Cover the pan tightly with foil and a lid and bake for 25 minutes so the rice finishes cooking in the steam.
Rest for 10 minutes, then loosen the layers gently with a fork and serve with raita.

title: Dal Tadka
intro: Comforting yellow lentils finished with a sizzling pour of spiced ghee, garlic and chilli.
ingredients: 250 g (1¼ cups) split yellow lentils (toor or moong dal), rinsed
steps: Put the lentils in a saucepan with 900 ml (3¾ cups) water, the turmeric and salt. Bring to the boil, skim, then simmer for 25 to 30 minutes until the lentils collapse. Whisk briefly to make them creamy, adding water if too thick.

Heat half the ghee in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until golden, then stir in the tomatoes, green chilli, ground coriander and chilli powder and cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Stir this mixture into the lentils and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the lemon juice and most of the fresh coriander.

For the tadka, heat the remaining ghee in a small pan until very hot. Add the cumin seeds, mustard seeds, dried chillies and asafoetida, and as soon as they crackle add the garlic and fry for 30 seconds until golden.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal at the table, scatter with the remaining coriander and serve with rice or chapatis.

title: Chana Masala
intro: A hearty Punjabi chickpea curry in a tangy tomato and onion sauce sharpened with amchoor and lemon.
ingredients: 2 × 400 g (14 oz) tins chickpeas, drained and rinsed
1 tsp amchoor (dried mango powder) or juice of ½ lemon
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and sizzle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds. Add the onions and cook for 10 minutes until soft and golden brown.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chillies and cook for 2 minutes, then add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and a teaspoon of salt and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts to separate at the edges.
Tip in the chickpeas with 250 ml (1 cup) water and simmer for 15 minutes, crushing a few chickpeas against the side of the pan to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala and amchoor or lemon juice and check the seasoning.
Scatter with fresh coriander and serve with rice, bhatura or chapatis.

title: Vegetable Samosas
intro: Crisp triangular pastries stuffed with spiced potato and peas, fried until golden and blistered.
ingredients: 4 tbsp vegetable oil, plus extra for deep-frying
500 g (1 lb) floury potatoes, boiled and peeled
steps: Mix the flour, salt and carom seeds, rub in the 4 tablespoons of oil until crumbly, then add about 100 ml (scant ½ cup) cold water a little at a time to form a firm dough. Knead for 2 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.

Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a frying pan and sizzle the cumin and coriander seeds for 20 seconds. Add the ginger and chillies, cook for 1 minute, then add the roughly crushed potatoes, peas, garam masala, turmeric, amchoor and salt. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stir in the coriander and cool.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Roll each into an oval about 18 cm long and cut it in half across the middle to give two half-moons.

Take one half, brush the straight edge with water, and fold it into a cone, pressing the seam to seal. Fill the cone two-thirds full with the potato mixture, brush the open edge with water and pinch it shut.

Heat oil in a deep pan to 160 °C (320 °F). Fry the samosas in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp, keeping the oil at a moderate heat so the pastry blisters rather than browns too fast.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve hot with tamarind or mint chutney.

title: Pork and Chive Dumplings (Jiaozi)
intro: Hand-pleated boiled dumplings with a juicy pork and garlic chive filling, served with a black vinegar dip.
ingredients: 300 g (2½ cups) plain flour, plus extra for dusting
400 g (14 oz) minced pork, not too lean
150 g (5 oz) garlic chives, finely chopped
3 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
Chinkiang black vinegar and chilli oil, to serve
steps: Stir the hot water into the flour with chopsticks until it clumps, then knead for 5 minutes into a smooth, firm dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

Mix the pork with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, salt and pepper. Beat in the cold water a tablespoon at a time, stirring in one direction until the mixture is sticky, then fold in the chives.
Roll the dough into a long rope and cut into about 40 pieces. Flatten each and roll into a thin 8 cm circle, keeping the centre a little thicker than the edges.

Place a heaped teaspoon of filling in the middle of a wrapper, fold it into a half-moon and pinch the centre shut, then make small pleats along one side, pressing them against the flat side to seal. Repeat, keeping the finished dumplings on a floured tray.

Bring a large pot of water to the boil. Add the dumplings in batches, stir once so they do not stick, and when the water returns to the boil add a cup of cold water. Repeat once more, then cook for about 2 minutes until the dumplings float and the wrappers look translucent, 8 to 10 minutes in all.
Lift out with a slotted spoon and serve with black vinegar and chilli oil for dipping.

title: Beef Rendang
intro: A dark, intensely spiced West Sumatran dish where beef cooks slowly until the coconut milk reduces to a rich, clinging paste.
ingredients: 1.2 kg (2⅔ lb) beef chuck or shin, cut into 4 cm chunks
6 to 8 dried red chillies, soaked, or 3 fresh red chillies
2 × 400 ml (14 fl oz) tins coconut milk
60 g (¾ cup) desiccated coconut, toasted until golden
2 tbsp palm sugar or soft brown sugar
1 cinnamon stick, 3 cloves and 3 star anise
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies, ginger, galangal and turmeric with a splash of water into a smooth paste.
Heat the oil in a wide heavy pan over medium heat and fry the paste with the cinnamon, cloves and star anise for 5 to 6 minutes until fragrant and starting to catch.
Add the beef and turn it in the paste for 3 to 4 minutes, then pour in the coconut milk and add the lemongrass, lime leaves, tamarind, sugar and salt. Bring to the boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 2 hours, stirring every 15 minutes or so, as the liquid slowly reduces and the beef becomes tender.
Stir in the toasted coconut and keep cooking for another 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring more often, as the sauce thickens, the oil separates and the beef turns dark brown.
In the last 15 minutes stir almost constantly so the thick paste fries in its own oil without burning. Remove the lemongrass and whole spices.
Serve with steamed rice; the flavour improves if the rendang rests overnight.

title: Nasi Goreng
intro: Indonesia's smoky sweet fried rice, darkened with kecap manis and crowned with a crisp-edged fried egg.
ingredients: 400 g (3 cups) cooked and chilled long-grain rice
150 g (5 oz) boneless chicken thigh, finely diced
Sliced cucumber, tomato and crispy fried shallots, to serve
steps: Pound or blend the shallots, garlic, chillies and shrimp paste into a rough paste.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a wok over high heat and fry the paste for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 minutes, then the prawns for 1 to 2 minutes until pink.
Add the cold rice and toss hard for 3 to 4 minutes, breaking up any clumps, until it is hot through and beginning to catch.
Pour in the kecap manis and soy sauce and keep tossing for 1 minute until the rice is evenly brown and glossy. Stir in the spring onions.
In a separate pan, fry the eggs in the remaining oil over high heat until the edges are crisp and the yolks are still soft.
Pile the rice onto plates, top each with a fried egg and serve with cucumber, tomato and fried shallots.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
intro: Pan-seared chicken thighs lacquered in a sweet soy, mirin and sake glaze.
ingredients: 4 boneless, skin-on chicken thighs (about 500 g / 1 lb)
Steamed rice, sesame seeds and sliced spring onion, to serve
steps: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger and garlic together until the sugar dissolves.
Pat the chicken dry and prick the skin a few times with a fork so the glaze can get in and the skin stays flat.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and lay the chicken in skin side down. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes without moving until the skin is deep golden, then turn and cook for 4 minutes more.

Pour off most of the fat, then add the sauce to the pan. Simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, turning the chicken and spooning the sauce over, until it reduces to a sticky glaze and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest for 2 minutes, slice, and serve over rice with the remaining glaze, sesame seeds and spring onion.

title: Chicken Katsu Curry
intro: Crunchy panko-crumbed chicken cutlets with a mild, glossy Japanese curry sauce over rice.
ingredients: 1 tbsp each soy sauce and honey
steps: For the sauce, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the carrot, potato, garlic and ginger and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in 2 tablespoons of the flour, the curry powder and garam masala and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the stock, then add the soy sauce and honey.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are soft and the sauce is thick. Blend until smooth if you prefer, and keep warm.

Put the chicken breasts between two sheets of baking paper and bash them to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season, then dip each in the remaining flour, then egg, then panko, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Heat 1 cm of oil in a large frying pan to 170 °C (340 °F). Fry the chicken two at a time for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on kitchen paper.
Slice the katsu into strips, lay over bowls of rice and pour the curry sauce alongside.

title: Tom Yum Goong
intro: A hot and sour Thai prawn soup sharp with lime, lemongrass and galangal.
ingredients: 1 litre (4¼ cups) chicken or prawn stock
3 stalks lemongrass, bruised and cut into 5 cm pieces
400 g (14 oz) raw prawns, peeled with tails on, shells kept
200 g (7 oz) oyster or straw mushrooms, halved
2 tbsp Thai roasted chilli paste (nam prik pao)
steps: Bring the stock to the boil with the prawn shells, lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and chillies. Simmer for 10 minutes so the aromatics infuse, then scoop out the shells.
Add the mushrooms and tomatoes and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce, sugar and chilli paste, then add the prawns and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until they are just pink and curled.
Take the pan off the heat and add the lime juice, tasting and adjusting so the soup is sharply sour, hot and lightly salty.
Ladle into bowls, leaving the lemongrass and galangal behind or warning diners not to eat them, and finish with coriander.

title: Chicken Adobo
intro: The Philippines' best-loved braise, with chicken simmered in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and black pepper.
ingredients: 1 kg (2¼ lb) bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
120 ml (½ cup) cane or white vinegar
1 tsp whole black peppercorns, lightly crushed
Steamed rice and sliced spring onion, to serve
steps: Put the chicken in a bowl with the vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, peppercorns and bay leaves and leave to marinate for 30 minutes or up to overnight.
Lift the chicken out, reserving the marinade. Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat and brown the pieces for 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Pour in the marinade and the water, add the sugar and bring to the boil without stirring for the first 2 minutes so the vinegar's sharpness cooks off.
Cover, reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes, turning the chicken halfway, until tender.
Remove the lid and simmer for 10 minutes more until the sauce has reduced and thickened enough to coat the chicken.
Serve over steamed rice with the sauce spooned over and a little spring onion on top.
